text.text_excerpt: Nice little store in the Quarter. Has a hot food/deli/pizza counter. Some basic groceries...all you need in a corner store! I ordered a Gavillacio sandwich on chiabatta bread. Never heard of it before, but it sounded good. Genoa salami, smoked bufala mozzarella, arugula, artichokes, sweet roasted peppers. I ended up riding my bike 9 miles home before eating it, so it was a little wet on the bottom from the arugula, artichoke, and peppers, but no big deal. I put it on a plate upside down in the fridge for 10 mins and all was good. It has an Interesting flavor, super tasty mozzerella and salami, the roasted peppers add a savory component, the artichoke made it a little salty/tart, a bit of ...

matassa's cares. I order wine, gumbo, etc from my workplace often. love the seafood gumbo! love the chicken po boy. the last time I called they were out of the Chardonnay I wanted (btw this is for the customers you guys i promise I'm not usually a work wino) and they called me back and talked me through all their available options, prices, and sizes. lots of places would've just brought beringer lol (or whatever they found to be comparable). it's usually cheaper than Verti, although I love them too.

OK, disclaimer : I'm friends with them, and I live in the neighborhood, so delete a star if you don't know the family. As far as New Orleans corner groceries go, this is the classic. They have everything, and they deliver ! If it's not in stock, they will order it for you. Above average wine selection for a small store...comes in handy when you're eating in the neighborhood at a BYOB restaurant. The best, best, best fried chicken I've ever had, ever...really, the best. Did you catch that ? Order the fried chicken. This place also sells my household's absolute favorite king cakes during carnival season.
